title: Balance factor
summary: Left height minus right height, at every node. Anything outside -1 to +1 needs a rotation.

checkpoints.text: A plain binary search tree, built without any balancing. The left side has grown deeper than the right.
The first node printed is the leaf 5. Both of its sides are empty, so its balance factor is 0 - 0 = 0.
The root, 40: its left side is 3 levels tall and its right side 1, so its balance is 3 - 1 = +2. An AVL tree allows only -1, 0 or +1, so this node needs fixing.
The tree leans left at 40, and the new value 5 went into the left side of its left child: a left-left case, fixed by one right rotation.
20 moved up and 40 came down to its right. 20's old right child, 30, was handed over to 40 as its left child: everything in it is between 20 and 40, so the order is kept.
Before: 5(0) 10(1) 20(1) 30(0) 40(2) 60(0). After: every node is between -1 and +1. Only pointers changed; no value moved.
